title: The specimen shelf: keep an individual's genetics, put it back as itself or drifted
question: Clone and mutate are one dial here, not two buttons: 0 is that exact individual again, 1 is as different as its own child would have been. Is that the right way to offer it, or do you want CLONE and MUTATE as separate verbs?
context_md:
**What it does.** You can now save the genetics of anything alive in the box, keep it in a jar that outlives the box, and put it back -- as itself, or bred forward. Plants and ants both. Two new tools on the bar (`KEEP` M, `FREE` ,) and a rack page (`G`).

**Where it sits.** First of the two gaps the round-three handoff names -- *'there is no save; a parameter he changes and cannot keep is a toy'* -- and the same sentence was true of an animal. The other gap, species parameters not being reachable at runtime, is untouched.

**The dial is the thing I want judged.** One brood applies the engine's own per-birth mutation once -- no new rate is invented and none is calibrated -- so the unit means something: three broods is a great-grandchild's worth of drift. The alternative is a CLONE button and a MUTATE button, which is the binary this project keeps ruling against.

**Already checked, so don't spend the answer on it:** the released individual is bit-identical at 0 broods (guarded both kingdoms); a release books as a founder, never as a birth; a jar never overwrites another; a plant's whole growth program travels in the jar, not just its numbers.

**Known and not fixed:** `PROMOTE` (jar -> a species file the game can load) is creatures only, and still needs a hand-drawn material before the promoted animal will hatch. Both rows of the bar are now completely full.

items.caption: HERB was kept out of the bed, then COPY made HERB_2 three broods along. The parent stays armed so you can make siblings.
